title_en: Jinhua Municipal People's Procuratorate v. Hu Xiangzhen — fraud case
ruling_gist_en: The defendant, after borrowing money, privately changed the use of the loan and used it for other commercial activities. Moreover, to respond to the lender's demands for repayment, he instructed others to forge the company seal and receipts of the enterprise with which he claimed to be jointly developing the project. Since he did not have the purpose of illegal possession of the loan, his conduct does not constitute the crime of fraud. However, his act of instructing others to forge the company seal constitutes the crime of forging company seals under Article 280, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law.

full_text_en:
Jinhua City People's Procuratorate v. Hu Xiangzhen — Fraud Case

【Ruling Summary】

Where a defendant, after borrowing funds, privately changes the purpose of the borrowed funds by using them for other commercial activities, and, to deal with the creditor's demand for repayment, instructs others to forge the company seal and receipts of the enterprise that cooperated in developing the project with him, the defendant does not have the intent to illegally possess the borrowed funds and thus does not constitute the crime of fraud. However, his act of instructing others to forge a company seal constitutes the crime of forging company seals under Article 280, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law.

Criminal Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2003) Xing Ti Zi No. 4

Original defendant in the retrial: Hu Xiangzhen, also known as Hu Fangzhu, male, born on November 25, 1950, Han ethnicity, native of Yueqing City, Zhejiang Province, education level: two years of primary school, farmer and businessman, formerly General Manager and Legal Representative of Shanghai Hengfeng Zhiye Development Company, Chairman and General Manager of Yueqing High-Speed Passenger Ferry Co., Ltd., residing at Pengqiao Village, Xiangyang Town, Yueqing City. He was criminally detained on March 11, 1998, and arrested on April 18 of the same year. He is currently serving his sentence in the No. 6 Prison of Zhejiang Province.

Defense Counsel: Luo Yun, lawyer from Beijing Zhongbei Law Firm.

Defense Counsel: Pei Guangchuan, lawyer from Beijing Huiyuan Law Firm.

In the case of the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province hearing the criminal charges filed by the Jinhua City People's Procuratorate against the defendant Hu Xiangzhen for contract fraud, and the incidental civil action initiated by the plaintiff of the incidental civil action, Zhejiang Chaosanchao Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Chaosanchao), the court rendered the Criminal and Incidental Civil Judgment (1999) Jin Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 9 on March 26, 1999, finding the defendant Hu Xiangzhen guilty of fraud, sentencing him to life imprisonment, depriving him of political rights for life; ordering recovery of Hu Xiangzhen's fraud proceeds of RMB 65,743,200, and ordering Hu Xiangzhen to make restitution for the interest on the illegally obtained funds occupied, in the amount of RMB 27,316,882.80; and dismissing the claims of the plaintiff in the incidental civil action, Chaosanchao. After the judgment was announced, Hu Xiangzhen refused to accept it and appealed. The Zhejiang High People's Court rendered the Criminal Judgment (1999) Zhe Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 222 on October 10 of the same year, dismissing Hu Xiangzhen's appeal; setting aside the portion of the first-instance judgment ordering Hu Xiangzhen to make restitution for the interest on the illegally obtained funds occupied in the amount of RMB 27,316,882.80, while affirming the remainder. After the second-instance judgment became legally effective, Hu Xiangzhen still refused to accept it and filed a petition with this Court. This Court rendered the Retrial Decision (2002) Xing Jian Zi No. 18 on May 26, 2003, deciding to conduct a trial de novo of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel according to law and has now concluded the trial.

The first-instance judgment of the Jinhua Intermediate People's Court found the following facts:

On January 8, 1995, the defendant Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Shanghai Hengfeng Zhiye Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Hengfeng Company), signed a Joint Development Agreement for the Wubei Indoor Vegetable Market Project (hereinafter referred to as the Wubei Project) with Shanghai Asia Food Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Asia Group), stipulating that Hengfeng Company would be responsible for all funds for the construction of the project, totaling approximately RMB 180 million. The Wubei Project was to be specifically developed by Shanghai Asia Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Asia Real Estate), a subsidiary of Asia Group. On February 17 of the same year, Hengfeng Company paid RMB 1 million to Asia Group and thereafter made no further payments for the project, and Asia Group did not actually operate the Wubei Project. On June 3, 1997, the Jing'an District Government of Shanghai issued an order to withdraw the land use rights for the project.

Between February and September 1995, the defendant Hu Xiangzhen borrowed a total of RMB 30 million from the Jinhua Auction Center of Zhejiang Jincheng Auction House (hereinafter referred to as Jinhua Auction Center), which was used by Hengfeng Company to repay loans and for daily expenses. In November of the same year, to deal with the demand for repayment of the overdue loan by Cheng Weimin, manager of Jinhua Auction Center, and others, Hu Xiangzhen arranged for someone to privately engrave a "Financial Seal of Asia Real Estate Development Company" and instructed the company accountant to forge five receipts showing that Asia Real Estate had received RMB 31 million from Hengfeng Company as investment in the Wubei Project, thereby deceiving Cheng Weimin and others.

In early 1996, after being introduced by Cheng Weimin and others and conducting an on-site inspection, Chaosanchao prepared to take over the Wubei Project. On February 5 of the same year, Asia Group, Hengfeng Company, and Chaosanchao signed the Wubei Project Joint Development (Investment) Agreement. On the same day, the defendant Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Hengfeng Company, also signed an agreement with Chaosanchao for the transfer of partial investment beneficial rights in the Wubei Project. Thus, Hu Xiangzhen transferred to Chaosanchao, by agreement, the non-existent investment of Hengfeng Company of RMB 31 million in the Wubei Project. Between February and March of the same year, Chaosanchao paid Hengfeng Company a total of RMB 35,743,200 for the transfer of the Wubei Project, of which RMB 33,377,200 was paid, upon the instruction of Hu Xiangzhen and others, to the Wucheng Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Wucheng) and the Jinhua Auction Center to repay loans.

On May 30, 1994, the Catholic Diocese of Shanghai signed an agreement with Shanghai Dazhonghua Electrical Appliance Store (hereinafter referred to as Dazhonghua Store) to plan the construction of the Dazhonghua Electrical Appliance Building (hereinafter referred to as Dazhonghua Building). On July 8 of the same year, Dazhonghua Store signed a joint construction agreement with Shanghai Kaicheng Real Estate Management Company (hereinafter referred to as Kaicheng Company) for the joint development of the Dazhonghua Building. On June 28 of the same year, Kaicheng Company signed an agreement with Hengfeng Company for the joint development and construction of the Dazhonghua Building, stipulating that Kaicheng Company would be responsible for the project's planning, project approval, construction, and all supporting work, and Hengfeng Company would be responsible for raising construction funds of RMB 35 million. After completion, Kaicheng Company would receive 80 square meters of floor area, and Hengfeng Company would receive 3,000 square meters. On July 20 of the same year, Hengfeng Company signed an agreement with the Material Company of Jinhua Yinshi Industrial General Company (hereinafter referred to as Yinshi Company), stipulating that Yinshi Company would raise RMB 20 million for the Dazhonghua project. On July 23 of the same year, Yinshi Company paid RMB 20 million as agreed. On December 28 of the same year, the Dazhonghua Building was completed. After the Spring Festival of 1996, due to a failure to reach an agreement with Dazhonghua Store on the division of property rights in the building, Kaicheng Company filed a lawsuit against Dazhonghua Store with the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court on April 16.

In February 1996, in order to raise funds to purchase a high-speed passenger ferry, the defendant Hu Xiangzhen intended to transfer the Dazhonghua Building, to which he had no ownership rights, to Chaosanchao, and concealed from Yang Baiqun, General Manager of Chaosanchao, the fact that Hengfeng Company had signed an agreement with Yinshi Company. On May 1 of the same year, Luo Qiming, Deputy General Manager of Hengfeng Company, on the instruction of Hu Xiangzhen, signed an agreement with Chaosanchao for the transfer of property rights in the Dazhonghua Building. After the agreement was signed, Chaosanchao paid Hengfeng Company RMB 20 million on May 3 and May 14 of the same year, as agreed, and then, at the request of Hu Xiangzhen, paid an additional RMB 10 million to Hengfeng Company on May 24. Thus, Hu Xiangzhen received a total of RMB 30 million from Chaosanchao as payment for the transfer of the Dazhonghua Building property rights, of which RMB 27 million was used by Hu Xiangzhen to purchase the high-speed passenger ferry. To date, Chaosanchao has been unable to obtain the property rights to the Dazhonghua Building. On March 15, 1998, the Jinhua Public Security Bureau seized and sealed the Fangzhu high-speed passenger ferry owned by Yueqing High-Speed Passenger Ferry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Passenger Ferry Company).

In summary, the defendant Hu Xiangzhen, by concealing the truth or fabricating facts and using the method of signing agreements with Chaosanchao for the transfer of the Wubei Project and the Dazhonghua Building, defrauded Chaosanchao of a total of RMB 65,743,200. As of January 10, 1999, Chaosanchao suffered an interest loss of RMB 27,316,882.80.

The first-instance judgment held that the defendant Hu Xiangzhen, with the intent of illegal possession, fabricated facts, concealed the truth, and deceived others to obtain their property in the course of entering into contracts with others, and his conduct constituted the crime of fraud. The amount of property defrauded was exceptionally large, the circumstances were particularly serious, and he should be punished according to law. The proceeds of the crime should be recovered by the public security organs according to law, and Hu Xiangzhen should make restitution for the interest on the illegally obtained funds he occupied. The incidental civil claims of Chaosanchao did not fall within the scope of Article 36 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China and were therefore not supported.

The second-instance judgment of the Zhejiang High People's Court held that the facts of this case were clear and the evidence was reliable and sufficient. The defenses and arguments of the defendant Hu Xiangzhen and his defense counsel that the case constituted an economic contract dispute or civil fraud were found, upon examination, to be inconsistent with the facts and were not accepted. Hu Xiangzhen, with the intent of illegal possession, used the method of fabricating facts and concealing the truth to defraud others of their money and property, and his conduct constituted the crime of fraud. The amount was exceptionally large, the circumstances were particularly serious, and he should be severely punished according to law. The first-instance judgment was correct in conviction, appropriate in sentencing, and the trial procedure was lawful, except that the portion ordering Hu Xiangzhen to make restitution for the interest on the illegally obtained funds he occupied was improper and should be corrected.

In the retrial, the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen and his defense counsel raised the following defenses and arguments: 1. Hu Xiangzhen had invested RMB 51 million in the Wubei Project (including a bank deposit certificate of RMB 50 million). His purpose in presenting copies of the receipts showing an investment of RMB 31 million when transferring the beneficial rights of the Wubei Project to Chaosanchao was not to illegally possess the funds of that company, but rather to induce the company to invest in the Wubei Project as soon as possible and to achieve early success in cooperation. Hu Xiangzhen had fully invested funds in the Dazhonghua Building. Although he concealed the fact that there was a dispute over property rights and that a lawsuit had been filed on that matter at the time of the transfer, according to the civil judgment rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court, Hu Xiangzhen could obtain the return of over RMB 30 million in investment funds, which was sufficient to offset the RMB 30 million transfer payment made by Chaosanchao. Therefore, Hu Xiangzhen's conduct did not constitute the crime of fraud. 2. Article 152 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (1979) only provided for individual crimes, but throughout this case, Hu Xiangzhen acted in the name of his company, Hengfeng, externally in cooperative development activities, and all economic transactions were entered into and exited through the company's accounts. Therefore, Hu Xiangzhen's conduct also did not constitute the crime of fraud.

Upon retrial, this Court finds the following facts:

On April 14, 1994, Hengfeng Company was registered with the Qingpu County Administration for Industry and Commerce of Shanghai and obtained a business license as a legal person enterprise. The economic nature of the company was a collective enterprise, with registered capital of RMB 5 million. The original defendant in the retrial, Hu Xiangzhen, served as General Manager and Legal Representative.

Between May 1993 and December 1994, Asia Group completed a series of approval procedures with relevant administrative authorities, including a permit for construction land use, for the construction of the new Wubei Project. On January 1, 1995, Asia Group issued a power of attorney, fully authorizing Asia Real Estate, a subsidiary of the group, to plan, construct, develop, and operate the Wubei Project and other projects.

On January 8, 1995, the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Hengfeng Company, signed the Wubei Project Joint Development Agreement with Asia Group. The agreement stipulated that Asia Group would be responsible for relocation work, providing the relevant administrative approval documents, and handling all preliminary procedures for development and construction; and that Hengfeng Company would bear all costs and expenses for the project construction, estimated at approximately RMB 180 million. For profit distribution, Asia Group was to receive 13.15% (4,000 square meters), and Hengfeng Company was to receive 86.85%, with ownership rights to be obtained proportionally. On January 18, January 25, and May 10 of the same year, Hengfeng Company and Asia Group successively signed three supplementary agreements, including a provision that if Hengfeng Company's annual return on investment fell below 20%, Asia Group would provide compensation; Hengfeng Company would compensate Asia Group in the amount of RMB 1 million; and the profit distribution was changed so that, out of the 30,400 square meters of buildable floor area, Asia Group would receive 6.58% (2,000 square meters, of which 50% would be on the ground floor), and Hengfeng Company would receive 93.42%. On February 17 of the same year, Hengfeng Company paid Asia Real Estate RMB 1 million as compensation for the Wubei Project, and made no further capital contributions thereafter.

In February 1995, the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen reached an agreement with Cheng Weimin, Deputy President of ICBC Wucheng and Manager of Jinhua Auction Center, and Shang Zheng, Deputy Manager of Jinhua Auction Center, whereby, through Hu Xiangzhen's introduction, ICBC Wucheng would borrow RMB 50 million from the Wenzhou Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, and then lend RMB 25 million of that amount to Hu Xiangzhen. In February and April of the same year, Jinhua Auction Center, as agreed, lent RMB 25 million to Hengfeng Company in the form of payments for the purchase of commercial housing (the Wubei Project) under a contract. In September of the same year, Hu Xiangzhen again contacted Cheng Weimin and borrowed RMB 5 million from Jinhua Auction Center in the form of a property purchase agreement (for the Dazhonghua Building) (with RMB 4 million actually paid, and RMB 1 million withheld as interest on the earlier RMB 25 million loan). Hu Xiangzhen used the above loans from Jinhua Auction Center for Hengfeng Company to repay loans and for daily expenses.

After the above loans became due, Cheng Weimin repeatedly demanded repayment from the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen. To deal with the demands of Cheng Weimin and others, Hu Xiangzhen falsely claimed that all the loans from Jinhua Auction Center had been invested in the Wubei Project and could not be repaid for the time being. In November 1995, Hu Xiangzhen further instructed the company accountant, Wei Jianfang, to falsely prepare receipts showing that Asia Real Estate had received RMB 30 million from Hengfeng Company as investment in the Wubei Project, and stamped them with the privately engraved "Financial Seal of Asia Real Estate Development Company." He then had copies of the forged receipts made and delivered to Cheng Weimin.

Between November and December 1995, to help the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen raise funds, Cheng Weimin brought two blank unit time deposit certificates from ICBC Wucheng to Shanghai and gave them to Hu Xiangzhen. Hu Xiangzhen filled in one blank certificate to show that Hengfeng Company had deposited RMB 50 million, with a deposit period from October 15, 1995 to April 15, 1996, and pledged it to Asia Real Estate. On January 31, 1996, Hu Xiangzhen issued a letter of authorization stating: "The company's deposit of RMB 50 million will be directly remitted upon maturity to the account of Shanghai Asia Food Group Corporation for relocation expenses." On the same day, Asia Real Estate issued a receipt acknowledging receipt of RMB 50 million as relocation fees from Hengfeng Company. In October 1996, Cheng Weimin recovered the deposit certificate from Hu Xiangzhen.

In early 1996, to recover the RMB 30 million lent to Hengfeng Company, Cheng Weimin contacted Yang Baiqun, General Manager of Chaosanchao, and told him that ICBC Wucheng and Hengfeng Company had been involved in the Wubei Project in Shanghai and had already invested over RMB 30 million. Now, due to policy, banks could no longer engage in real estate development, and ICBC Wucheng wanted to withdraw its funds, but the project had a relatively good rate of return and was to be transferred to Chaosanchao, with project funds to be provided by ICBC Wucheng. Yang Baiqun, along with Pan Shunchu, Deputy General Manager of Chaosanchao, and others, went to Shanghai to inspect the Wubei Project on-site. After the inspection, they believed the location was good, a prime location, and the project was feasible. During this time, Hu Xiangzhen discussed the specific details of the transfer of the Wubei Project with Yang Baiqun and provided Yang Baiqun with copies of various approval documents for the Wubei Project and the forged receipts showing Hengfeng Company's investment. Upon returning from Shanghai, Yang Baiqun and Pan Shunchu specifically convened a meeting with the company's directors, Yang Baiwei, Tang Qun, Zhou Guoyou, and Zhang Shenghua, to study the matter. They believed that the project's rate of return was good, that funds would be supported by ICBC Wucheng, and that Chaosanchao had been nurtured by ICBC Wucheng and needed to help the bank. They unanimously agreed to take over the Wubei Project.

On February 5, 1996, the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Hengfeng Company, signed the Wubei Project Joint Development (Investment) Agreement with Asia Group and Chaosanchao in Shanghai. The agreement stipulated that the investment obligations originally assumed by Hengfeng Company would be jointly borne by Hengfeng Company and Chaosanchao, with an investment ratio of 1:5 between the two companies. On the same day, Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Hengfeng Company, also signed an agreement with Chaosanchao for the transfer of partial investment beneficial rights in the Wubei Project. The agreement stipulated that Hengfeng Company's original investment of RMB 31 million and the benefits derived therefrom were all transferred to Chaosanchao. In February and March of 1996, Chaosanchao paid Hengfeng Company a total of RMB 35,743,200 for the transfer of the Wubei Project as agreed, of which RMB 33,377,200 was paid, upon the instruction of Hu Xiangzhen and others, to ICBC Wucheng and the Jinhua Auction Center to repay loans on behalf of Hengfeng Company. During the same period, Chaosanchao also paid Asia Real Estate RMB 38 million for the Wubei Project.

On June 3, 1997, because no development had been carried out on the relevant plots of land for the Wubei Project within two years of the land use approval, the Jing'an District Government of Shanghai lawfully withdrew the land use rights of Asia Group and canceled the construction land use permit.

On May 30, 1994, the Catholic Diocese of Shanghai, on behalf of the Catholic Commission of Jiangxi (Zhejiang) Province, signed an agreement with Dazhonghua Store. The agreement stipulated that Dazhonghua Store would fund the demolition and reconstruction of properties located at 461-473 Jinling East Road, 114-126 Zhejiang South Road, and 24-27 Lane 128, Zhejiang South Road (these properties were part of the Catholic Shoushan Church estate, with ownership belonging to the Catholic Commissions of Jiangxi and Zhejiang Provinces), to build the Dazhonghua Building. After the new building was completed, each party would own 50% of the property rights. On July 8 of the same year, Dazhonghua Store signed a joint construction agreement and supplementary agreement with Kaicheng Company for the Dazhonghua Building. The agreement stipulated that Dazhonghua Store would be responsible for planning, project approval, utility hookups (water, electricity, gas, etc.), and related supporting work, while Kaicheng Company would provide full investment. After the building was completed, from the ground floor upward, a portion of the property rights would belong to the church, and the remaining portion would belong to Kaicheng Company. Dazhonghua Store would have the right to use parts of the ground floor and second floor for commercial purposes.

After learning that Kaicheng Company lacked funds to develop the Dazhonghua Building, the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen, on behalf of Hengfeng Company, negotiated with Kaicheng Company. On June 28, 1994, the two parties signed an agreement for the joint development and construction of the Dazhonghua Building, under which Kaicheng Company was responsible for planning, project approval, construction, and all supporting work, and Hengfeng Company was responsible for raising construction funds of RMB 35 million on schedule. After the building was completed, Kaicheng Company would receive 800 square meters of floor area, and Hengfeng Company would receive 3,000 square meters (including 1,580 square meters of permanent right-of-use space on the second, third, and fourth floors, and 1,420 square meters of title-ownership space on the fifth floor and above). Due to a lack of development and construction funds, on July 20 of the same year, Hu Xiangzhen, after being introduced by others, signed an agreement on behalf of Hengfeng Company with Yinshi Company in Shanghai for the joint construction of the Dazhonghua Building. The agreement stipulated that Yinshi Company would be responsible for raising RMB 20 million, to be remitted in a lump sum to Kaicheng Company as designated by Hengfeng Company. The funds would have a 180-day usage period, after which Hengfeng Company guaranteed to repay Yinshi Company the principal of RMB 20 million plus RMB 3 million in interest. After the project was completed and sales were made, after Hengfeng Company paid necessary expenses, the economic benefits generated or the remaining property would be split 50-50 between the two parties. On July 21 of the same year, Yinshi Company paid RMB 20 million to Hengfeng Company as agreed. Shortly thereafter, because he still lacked funds for the development of the Dazhonghua Building, Hu Xiangzhen borrowed an additional RMB 10 million from Yinshi Company. Between July and November of the same year, Hengfeng Company paid a total of RMB 35 million to Kaicheng Company as a participation contribution for the Dazhonghua Building. In December of the same year, the Dazhonghua Building was completed.

1996年4月11日，上海市房产管理局颁发沪房市共字第00476号房屋共有权证，确认大中华商厦为江西省天主教教务委员会和大中华商店共有，共有份额双方各占50%。开城公司于同年4月16日向上海市第二中级人民法院起诉大中华商店和上海电子商厦总公司（以下简称商厦总公司），要求大中华商店移交大中华商厦2248.616平方米的产权房，并由商厦总公司承担连带责任。

胡祥祯因客轮公司购买高速客轮缺少资金，欲将大中华商厦转让给超三超公司。经过商谈，并经程伟民等人做工作，1996年5月1日，恒丰公司副总经理罗启明受胡祥祯委托代表恒丰公司与超三超公司在金华签订了大中华商厦房地产权转让协议。协议约定恒丰公司将大中华商厦2-7层的房地产权转让给超三超公司，总建筑面积约4000平方米（上下正负不超过100平方米），价格按14000元/平方米计算；恒丰公司负责办理所转让房地产权的过户手续，过户手续办理时间为1996年5月30日前；正式签约后十五天内由超三超公司付给恒丰公司人民币2000万元作为定金，其余房款在年底前后付清。按照协议，超三超公司于1996年5月3日和14日共付给恒丰公司人民币2000万元作为定金。同年5月24日，胡样祯因购买高速客轮急需资金，要求超三超公司提前支付人民币1000万元，并在明知肯定办不好房产过户手续的情况下，向杨佰群允诺5月30日前可以办好过户手续。杨佰群同意后又付给恒丰公司人民币1000万元。至此，恒丰公司共收到超三超公司支付的大中华商厦转让款人民币3000万元，其中2700万元用于购买高速客轮，其余款项用于向金华拍卖中心偿还借款等。

大中华商厦建成后，恒丰公司曾向开城公司催办大中华商厦中该公司应得部分房屋权证。

1998年3月15日，金华市公安局决定对方铸号高速客轮中胡祥祯所占资产予以扣押、查封。

1998年12月29日，上海市第二中级人民法院作出（1996）沪二中民初字第46号民事判决。该判决认为，开城公司与大中华商店签订的联建协议中涉及土地使用权的转让及建设项目的变更，且该土地为国有划拨土地，开城公司与大中华商店签订联建协议后未按规定办理报批手续及土地使用权变更登记手续，违反了我国房地产开发经营的有关法律规定，应认定协议无效。据此判决大中华商店返还开城公司36563171.62元并支付相应利息，大中华商店因系独立的企业法人，故商厦总公司对大中华商店不承担连带责任。开城公司不服，提出上诉。上海市高级人民法院于1999年3月25日作出（1999）沪高民终字第58号民事判决，驳回上诉，维持原判。

以上事实，有原审被告人胡样祯的供述，证人杨佰群、潘顺初、程伟民、商正、罗启明、曹雪琴、卫建芳、黄培义、丁近初、裘保成、吴剑强、李钢、华洪源等人的证言，有关行政机关的批复、意见书、通知，建设用地规划许可证、建筑工程执照、建设工程竣工规划验收合格证明、房屋共有权证，及有关协议书、委托书、转帐支票、汇票委托书、进帐单、借款条、收条、收据等书证，伪造的印章、收据，公安机关提取笔录、印章印文鉴定结论、笔迹检验鉴定结论、扣押、查封决定书、解除扣押查封通知书，方铸号高速客轮和大中华商厦照片，有关会计师事务所出具的审计报告，恒丰公司营业执照，上海市第二中级人民法院和上海市高级人民法院民事判决书等证据证实，足以认定。

本院认为：原审被告人胡祥祯在将乌北工程转让给超三超公司的过程中，虽然客观上有指使他人伪造亚细亚房产公司收到恒丰公司投资款收据等欺诈行为，但在上海市静安区政府收回土地使用权并注销建设用地许可证以前，乌北工程是经有关行政机关批准真实存在的，恒丰公司已向该工程投入人民币100万元；乌北工程最终下马主要是由于市房地局不允许拆迁等原因，胡祥祯转让时并不知道该工程会下马；胡祥祯派人私刻亚细亚房产公司财务专用章，并指使他人伪造亚细亚房产公司收到恒丰公司投资款收据，借以表明其已将金华拍卖中心的借款投入乌北工程的行为，主要目的是为了应付程伟民等人催讨债务；超三超公司决定接手乌北工程并帮助金华拍卖中心收回借款，主要是因为程伟民向杨佰群做了工作，以及超三超公司经实地考察后认为乌北工程有利可图，并且考虑到超三超公司是靠程伟民所在银行扶持起来的，要帮助程伟民；超三超公司支付转让款的流向清楚，没有证据证实胡祥祯有将转让款个人占有或者挥霍等行为；恒丰公司投资建成了大中华商厦并购买了方铸号高速客轮，具有较强的经济实力和一定的履约能力，非“皮包”或“空壳”公司。原审被告人胡祥祯在为客轮公司购买高速客轮而向超三超公司转让大中华商厦的过程中，虽然客观上也实施了一些欺诈和违法行为，但恒丰公司依约向大中华商厦投入人民币3500万元，大中华商厦亦实际建成，根据协议，恒丰公司可以获得3000平方米的产权房和永久使用权房；收到超三超公司转让款后，恒丰公司曾向开城公司催办有关房屋权证；后上海市两级法院的民事判决认定开城公司与大中华商店签订的有关协议无效，开城公司没有获得大中华商厦产权，以致恒丰公司亦无法办理相应的房产过户手续，并不是胡祥祯当时所能认识到的；胡祥祯获得的转让款主要用于购买方铸号高速客轮，流向清楚。

综上，认定原审被告人胡祥祯在上述行为中具有非法占有他人财物目的的证据不足，其行为不构成诈骗罪。原一、二审判决对胡祥祯以诈骗罪定罪量刑不当，应予纠正。胡祥祯及其辩护人提出的其行为不构成诈骗罪的主要辩解和辩护意见成立，应予采纳。

原审被告人胡祥祯的行为虽不构成诈骗罪，但其派人私刻亚细亚房产公司财务专用章，扰乱了公共秩序，其行为已构成伪造公司印章罪。且胡祥祯利用私刻的财务专用章，指使他人伪造亚细亚房产公司收到恒丰公司乌北工程投资款收据，对超三超公司决定接手乌北工程并签订转让协议、支付转让款具有一定影响，情节严重，应依法惩处。

依照《中华人民共和国刑事诉讼法》第二百零五条第二款、第二百零六条、《最高人民法院关于执行〈中华人民共和国刑事诉讼法〉若干问题的解释》第三百一十二条第（四）项和《中华人民共和国刑法》第十二条第一款、第二百八十条第二款的规定，判决如下：

一、撤销浙江省高级人民法院（1999）浙法刑终字第222号刑事判决；

二、原审被告人胡祥祯犯伪造公司印章罪，判处有期徒刑三年（刑期从判决执行之日起计算。判决执行以前先行羁押的，羁押一日折抵刑期一日，即自1998年3月11日起至2001年3月10日止）。

本判决送达后即发生法律效力。

审　判　长　李　彤

审　判　员　杨世伟

代理审判员　周　庆

二〇〇四年一月七日

书　记　员　韩　巍

［审判长简介］

李彤高级法官：1948年出生，哲学学士，1990年起任最高人民法院审判员。On April 11, 1996, the Shanghai Real Estate Administration issued the Housing Co-ownership Certificate, Hu Fang Shi Gong Zi No. 00476, confirming that the Great China Commercial Building was co-owned by the Jiangxi Provincial Catholic Affairs Commission and the Great China Store, with each party holding a 50% share. On April 16 of the same year, Kaicheng Company filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court against the Great China Store and Shanghai Electronics Commercial Building Corporation (hereinafter referred to as the Commercial Building Corporation), demanding that the Great China Store transfer the 2,248.616 square meters of property rights of the Great China Commercial Building and that the Commercial Building Corporation bear joint and several liability.

Hu Xiangzhen, because the Passenger Ship Company lacked funds to purchase high-speed passenger vessels, intended to transfer the Great China Commercial Building to Chaosanchao Company. After negotiations and through the efforts of Cheng Weimin and others, on May 1, 1996, Luo Qiming, Deputy General Manager of Hengfeng Company, entrusted by Hu Xiangzhen and acting on behalf of Hengfeng Company, signed an agreement with Chaosanchao Company in Jinhua for the transfer of the real estate rights of the Great China Commercial Building. The agreement stipulated that Hengfeng Company would transfer the real estate rights of Floors 2 to 7 of the Great China Commercial Building to Chaosanchao Company, with a total gross floor area of approximately 4,000 square meters (deviation not exceeding plus or minus 100 square meters), at a price calculated at RMB 14,000 per square meter; Hengfeng Company was responsible for handling the transfer procedures for the real estate rights, with the transfer completion deadline set before May 30, 1996; within fifteen days after the formal signing, Chaosanchao Company was to pay Hengfeng Company RMB 20 million as a deposit, with the remaining payment for the property to be settled around the end of the year. In accordance with the agreement, Chaosanchao Company paid a total of RMB 20 million to Hengfeng Company on May 3 and May 14, 1996, as a deposit. On May 24 of the same year, Hu Xiangzhen, urgently needing funds for the purchase of high-speed passenger vessels, requested Chaosanchao Company to advance payment of RMB 10 million, and, despite knowing that the property transfer procedures could certainly not be completed, promised Yang Baiqun that the transfer procedures could be completed by May 30. After agreeing, Yang Baiqun paid an additional RMB 10 million to Hengfeng Company. Thus, Hengfeng Company received a total of RMB 30 million from Chaosanchao Company as payment for the transfer of the Great China Commercial Building, of which RMB 27 million was used to purchase high-speed passenger vessels, and the remaining funds were used to repay loans to the Jinhua Auction Center, among other purposes.

After the Great China Commercial Building was completed, Hengfeng Company urged Kaicheng Company to expedite the issuance of the property rights certificate for the portion of the building that should belong to Hengfeng Company.

On March 15, 1998, the Jinhua Public Security Bureau decided to seize and seal the assets belonging to Hu Xiangzhen in the Fangzhu high-speed passenger vessel.

On December 29, 1998, the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (1996) Hu Er Zhong Min Chu Zi No. 46. The judgment held that the joint construction agreement between Kaicheng Company and the Great China Store involved the transfer of land use rights and changes to the construction project, and that the land was state-owned allocated land. After signing the joint construction agreement, Kaicheng Company and the Great China Store failed to go through the prescribed approval procedures and the registration procedures for the change of land use rights, which violated the relevant laws and regulations of China on real estate development and operation; therefore, the agreement should be deemed invalid. Accordingly, the court ordered the Great China Store to return RMB 36,563,171.62 to Kaicheng Company and pay corresponding interest, and, since the Great China Store was an independent enterprise legal person, the Commercial Building Corporation was not jointly and severally liable for the Great China Store. Kaicheng Company appealed the decision. The Shanghai High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (1999) Hu Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 58 on March 25, 1999, rejecting the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: the confession of the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen; the testimony of witnesses Yang Baiqun, Pan Shunchu, Cheng Weimin, Shang Zheng, Luo Qiming, Cao Xueqin, Wei Jianfang, Huang Peiyi, Ding Jinchu, Qiu Baocheng, Wu Jianqiang, Li Gang, Hua Hongyuan, among others; the approvals, opinions, and notices from relevant administrative organs; the Construction Land Planning Permit, the Construction Project License, the Certificate of Acceptance for Completion of Construction Project Planning, and the Housing Co-ownership Certificate; and related documentary evidence such as agreements, letters of authorization, transfer checks, bank draft authorizations, deposit slips, loan notes, receipts, and other vouchers; the forged seals and receipts; the extraction records by the public security organs, the forensic examination conclusions of the seal impressions, the handwriting examination conclusions, the decisions to seize and seal, the notice to remove the seizure and seal; photographs of the Fangzhu high-speed passenger vessel and the Great China Commercial Building; the audit report issued by the relevant accounting firm; the business license of Hengfeng Company; and the civil judgments of the Shanghai Second Intermediate People's Court and the Shanghai High People's Court. This evidence is sufficient for confirmation.

This Court holds: In the process of transferring the Wubei Project to Chaosanchao Company, although the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen objectively committed fraudulent acts such as instructing others to forge a receipt from Yazhou Real Estate Company acknowledging receipt of Hengfeng Company's investment funds, before the Shanghai Jing'an District Government withdrew the land use rights and revoked the construction land permit, the Wubei Project was a genuine project approved by the relevant administrative organs, and Hengfeng Company had invested RMB 1 million in the project. The ultimate suspension of the Wubei Project was mainly due to reasons such as the Municipal Bureau of Real Estate not permitting demolition and relocation; Hu Xiangzhen was unaware of the project's suspension at the time of the transfer. Hu Xiangzhen's actions of sending someone to privately engrave the financial seal of Yazhou Real Estate Company and instructing others to forge a receipt from Yazhou Real Estate Company acknowledging receipt of Hengfeng Company's investment funds, thereby attempting to show that he had invested the loan from the Jinhua Auction Center into the Wubei Project, were primarily intended to deal with the debt collection demands of Cheng Weimin and others. Chaosanchao Company's decision to take over the Wubei Project and help the Jinhua Auction Center recover the loan was mainly due to Cheng Weimin's efforts with Yang Baiqun, as well as Chaosanchao Company's conclusion after a site inspection that the Wubei Project was profitable, and also because Chaosanchao Company was supported by the bank where Cheng Weimin worked, so they wanted to help Cheng Weimin. The flow of the transfer payments made by Chaosanchao Company was clear, and there is no evidence to confirm that Hu Xiangzhen personally possessed or squandered the transfer funds. Hengfeng Company invested in the construction of the Great China Commercial Building and purchased the Fangzhu high-speed passenger vessel, demonstrating strong economic strength and certain performance capability; it was not a "briefcase" or "shell" company. In the process of transferring the Great China Commercial Building to Chaosanchao Company in order to purchase a high-speed passenger vessel for the Passenger Ship Company, although the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen objectively also committed some fraudulent and illegal acts, Hengfeng Company, in accordance with the agreement, invested RMB 35 million in the Great China Commercial Building, and the building was actually completed. According to the agreement, Hengfeng Company was entitled to 3,000 square meters of property rights housing and permanent usage rights housing. After receiving the transfer payment from Chaosanchao Company, Hengfeng Company urged Kaicheng Company to expedite the relevant property rights certificate. Subsequently, the civil judgments of the two levels of Shanghai courts determined that the relevant agreement between Kaicheng Company and the Great China Store was invalid, and Kaicheng Company did not obtain the property rights to the Great China Commercial Building, thus rendering Hengfeng Company unable to handle the corresponding property transfer procedures, a situation that Hu Xiangzhen could not have foreseen at the time. The transfer funds obtained by Hu Xiangzhen were mainly used to purchase the Fangzhu high-speed passenger vessel, and their flow was clear.

In summary, there is insufficient evidence to establish that the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen had the intent to unlawfully possess another person's property in the above-mentioned acts; his actions do not constitute the crime of fraud. The original first-instance and second-instance judgments' conviction and sentencing of Hu Xiangzhen for the crime of fraud were improper and should be corrected. The main defenses and arguments raised by Hu Xiangzhen and his defense counsel that his actions do not constitute the crime of fraud are valid and should be adopted.

Although the actions of the original defendant Hu Xiangzhen do not constitute the crime of fraud, his act of sending someone to privately engrave the financial seal of Yazhou Real Estate Company disturbed public order, and his actions have constituted the crime of forging company seals. Furthermore, Hu Xiangzhen used the privately engraved financial seal to instruct others to forge a receipt from Yazhou Real Estate Company acknowledging receipt of Hengfeng Company's investment funds for the Wubei Project, which had a certain influence on Chaosanchao Company's decision to take over the Wubei Project, sign the transfer agreement, and make the transfer payment. The circumstances are serious, and he should be punished according to law.

Pursuant to Article 205, paragraph 2, and Article 206 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 312, paragraph (4) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; and Article 12, paragraph 1, and Article 280, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Criminal Judgment (1999) Zhe Fa Xing Zhong Zi No. 222 of the Zhejiang High People's Court is reversed;

2. The original defendant Hu Xiangzhen is guilty of the crime of forging company seals and is sentenced to three years' imprisonment (the term of imprisonment shall be calculated from the date of execution of the judgment. Any period of detention prior to the execution of the judgment shall be offset against the term of imprisonment, one day of detention for one day of imprisonment, i.e., from March 11, 1998 to March 10, 2001).

This judgment is legally effective upon service.
